claims.text: As-received AlCrFeNiSi powder may have surface oxide layers.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi produces high thermal gradients.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi causes significant residual-stress accumulation.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF degrades the microstructure and mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating the LPBF substrate to 300–400°C, nominally about 350°C, will reduce thermal gradients and make the temperature distribution more uniform.
Substrate preheating reduces rapid quenching during solidification.
Rapid, nonequilibrium alloy processing can generate chemical short-range-order states distinct from equilibrium states.
Preheating AlCrFeNiSi during LPBF will reduce disturbances in chemical short-range order.
Preheating will produce a refined grain structure in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating will lower the dislocation density in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Sharp thermal differentials during LPBF induce high residual stresses and inhomogeneous phases.
Slower and more even cooling promotes microstructural uniformity and reduces cracking and internal stress.
AlCrFeNiSi miniature components built with substrate preheating will have lower residual stress than otherwise identical components built at room temperature.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will have higher yield strength than room-temperature-built controls.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will have greater ductility than room-temperature-built controls.
Substrate preheating will address processing complexity as well as stress-induced property degradation.
The proposed 300–400°C preheating window is applicable to LPBF components approximately 3–5 mm in characteristic dimension.
Scaling the intervention to larger components or different geometries may require additional parameter tuning.
